newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says it arrests members of exiled opposition.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it arrests members of exiled opposition.

text.p: Security forces in central Iran have arrested several members of an Iraq-based armed opposition group for stirring up disturbances, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Saturday.
It quoted the top intelligence official in Isfahan province as saying members of a terrorist team belonging to the Mujahideen Khalq were arrested on Thursday in Khomeinishahr.
The official said "the terrorist team had been engaged in stirring up disturbances and disorder among the people of the region".
He gave no details of the disturbances.
In Paris, the Mujahideen Khalq said in a statement residents in Khomeinishahr had staged large anti-government demonstrations since Tuesday.
The statement said there were many arrests but denied that those detained were members of the group. It said they were ordinary Iranians who sympathised with the Mujahideen.
The Mujahideen moved to Iraq in the early 1980s at the start of the eight-year-long Iraq-Iran war. They have mounted raids across the border into Iran, drawing Iranian reprisal attacks.
The Mujahideen Khalq, Iran's main exiled opposition group, has in recent months engaged in a spate of clashes with Iranian security troops in a cycle of violence unseen in recent years.
